items.title: John Abercrombie interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001
items.q: he taught arranging, which was sort of not really, almost in the style of Duke Ellington but that was his guy, you know so he loved Duke

ctx.x: Would you be able to put a percentage of what you play now and attribute any of it to your quote formal education?

Yeah I think so. I don’t know if I’d attribute it as much to the actual education that I got from specific teachers. I think it was more just the experience of being in school playing and developing and being around teachers and other students. And if anything I would attribute certain things of course to, there were a couple of teachers that were very important to me, Herb Pomeroy was one, he was a wonderful trumpet player but his main job at Berklee was to teach — he taught arranging, he taught advanced…

which were small ensembles of anywhere from like four to maybe six people. It could be a couple of horns for the rhythm section — I was in one that was just guitar and saxophone, piano, bass and drums. And it was wonderful because I had to function like a horn player. And I couldn’t read worth — I was terrible. I mean most guitar players will acknowledge that they, it’s a difficult instrument to read on. So I remember when they would first write tunes on the board and the saxophone player could read quite well.…
